clue.text: Provision for borrowing one pound in financial centre with nothing up front

indicators.note: says this piece goes at the very start of the answer, ahead of the rest

parts.note: FA, short for 'sweet FA', is British slang for nothing at all

indicators.note: the one and the pound are placed inside the financial centre's letters

parts.note: the City is London's financial district
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A lender offers a one-pound loan in the City, demanding no deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing up front' has nothing to do with deposits: FA is 'sweet FA', British slang for nothing at all. 'in' puts the one and the pound inside the financial centre, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A credit facility is an arrangement a bank makes letting a customer borrow money.

clue.text: Device to avoid duties that's bog standard?

definitions.meaning: a ship registered in a foreign country to escape taxes and regulations
the banner of the loo: a bog is British slang for a toilet and a standard is a banner

explanation.surface: A dodge to escape tax is described as completely ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bog standard' is British slang for plain and ordinary, but here a 'bog' is a toilet (a public one is a convenience) and a 'standard' is a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipowners register vessels in a foreign state to avoid levies, and the phrase splits into banner plus public toilet.

clue.text: See 1
Nigella Lawson's TV programme

indicators.note: the possessive here signals that the programme is held within the name

explanation.surface: This names a television cookery show presented by Nigella Lawson.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cookery show, but the end of 'Nigella' and the start of 'Lawson' hold an American legal drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The Los Angeles legal drama ran on US television from 1986 to 1994.

clue.text: TV programme — Baron, not mother, could be this

indicators.note: says these letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A sitcom title is hinted at: an aristocrat who isn't a mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges BARON, NOT and MOTHER. The answer is a British sitcom of the late 1970s and early 1980s about a widow who loses her estate.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC comedy series starring Penelope Keith was broadcast from 1979.

clue.text: Odd characters in ancient piece like vinegar

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and so on letters of the following words are picked out

explanation.surface: Some old relic gives off a sour, vinegary tang.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the odd-numbered letters of ANCIENT PIECE gives A, C, E, T, I, C.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic acid is the sour compound that gives vinegar its taste and smell.

clue.text: Tipple getting a neurotic drunk

indicators.note: being drunk leaves one disordered, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An anxious person gets drunk on a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange-flavoured French liqueur is a drink, or tipple.

clue.text: Boat turning belly up

indicators.note: turning up, in a down clue, means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: gut is another word for belly

explanation.surface: A boat capsizes, ending upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning ... up' suits a down clue: GUT reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A small powerful vessel that tows larger ships is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Coping with international's character

parts.note: a cap is a player chosen for an international side; with the 's the word becomes caps
tone means character or quality

explanation.surface: Someone is dealing with a foreign player's personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coping' looks like dealing with something, but it is the stone layer on top of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The top stone of a wall or structure forms its coping.

clue.text: Rooney's Portuguese World Cup opponent could be such an enthusiast

definitions.text: Rooney's Portuguese World Cup opponent could be such an enthusiast

parts.words: Rooney's Portuguese World Cup opponent could be such an enthusiast
parts.note: Wayne Rooney was sent off in the 2006 World Cup for treading on Portugal's Ricardo Carvalho, so the opponent gathered a stamp

explanation.surface: A footballer's opponent from Portugal is described as a keen hobbyist.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2006 England's Wayne Rooney stamped on Portugal's Carvalho, so the victim picked up a stamp, in the philatelist's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A philatelist gathers postage stamps, and Carvalho received one in the footballing sense.

clue.text: Girl left record

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman leaves behind a written account.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is a yearly chronicle, a historical record of events, usually seen in the plural.

clue.text: Accumulating rubbish collection on horse

parts.note: totting is British slang for scavenging saleable scrap from rubbish dumps
a rider on a horse is said to be up

explanation.surface: Someone gathers junk while sitting astride a horse, like a rag-and-bone man.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag-and-bone man, who collected scrap from a horse and cart, did the 'totting'; a jockey in the saddle is 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Totting up is adding things together into a running total, so building up a sum.

clue.text: However eccentric, Lord Mayor is best

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: L is a standard abbreviation for Lord
M is an abbreviation for Mayor

explanation.surface: A quirky Lord Mayor is said to be the finest, despite his oddities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges HOWEVER plus L and M. 'best' is a verb here, as in beating someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To best an opponent is to defeat them, and to crush or defeat utterly is the verb sense.

clue.text: Entice military police in Vietnam offensive

indicators.note: the military police are placed inside the name of the offensive

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was a 1968 North Vietnamese campaign

explanation.surface: Soldiers are lured into joining a wartime campaign in Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or attract someone with a promise, a direct synonym.

clue.text: What gives victory for striker over director

indicators.note: in a down clue the striker sits above the director

parts.note: a match is struck to light it
Michael Winner was a British film director

explanation.surface: A goal-scorer outshines the club's director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests a footballer, but it is a match; Michael Winner directed 'Death Wish'.
explanation.definitionFit: The decisive goal or player that secures a win in a game earns this label.

clue.text: He accounted for reactions as in third of laws

definitions.text: He accounted for reactions as in third of laws

parts.words: He accounted for reactions as in third of laws
parts.note: the third law of motion says every action has an equal and opposite reaction; the man who stated it is wanted

explanation.surface: A scientist explains how things react, according to the third rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reactions' sounds like chemistry or emotion, but it is the physics of forces: the third law of motion.
explanation.definitionFit: The English physicist formulated three laws of motion, the third concerning action and reaction.

clue.text: One maligns key people

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to slander is to malign

explanation.surface: Someone smears the most important people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like important, but a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A key is a small island, so its inhabitants are island dwellers.

clue.text: Held in muscles, rounded

indicators.note: the muscles come first and the rounded piece follows within the answer

parts.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles
orbed means made round like a sphere

explanation.surface: Someone is gripped in muscular arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Being engrossed means attention is gripped, so absorbed matches held.

clue.text: Should be fun galore — not half crazy

definitions.text: Should be fun galore — not half crazy

indicators.note: crazy means wildly disordered, so the gathered letters are jumbled
only half of the word is kept, its second three letters dropped

explanation.surface: Something meant to be great fun turns out barely half mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' cuts GALORE to GAL; 'crazy' then rearranges SHOULD, BE, FUN and GAL. The whole clue also describes a very entertaining person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is very funny company should give plenty of amusement, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: African with range of knowledge about New York area

indicators.note: the range of knowledge goes around the other letters

parts.note: ken is one's range of knowledge or understanding

explanation.surface: An African knows all about the New York region.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of an East African country with Nairobi as its capital.

clue.text: One of seven — or eleven or twelve?

definitions.meaning: one of the seven seas of the world
Danny's gang in the heist films titled with Eleven and Twelve carry this surname

explanation.surface: A puzzling count: is it one of seven, or of eleven or twelve?
explanation.walkthrough: The seven seas give one sense; the films 'Ocean's Eleven' and 'Ocean's Twelve' give the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Great bodies of salt water are counted as seven seas, and George Clooney's crew in the heist films bear that surname.

clue.text: I'd enable beggar finally to get stuffing

definitions.text: I'd enable beggar finally to get stuffing

indicators.note: stuffing something up means wrecking it, so the letters are jumbled
only the last letter of the word beggar is used

explanation.surface: Someone vows to help a beggar at last get a filling meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R from 'beggar'; 'stuffing' rearranges IDENABLE plus R. The whole clue describes the poverty line where food is the need.
explanation.definitionFit: People on the poverty line are those who can barely afford to eat, so filling the beggar's stomach fits.

clue.text: Material study supported by Institute of Management

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath

parts.note: a den is a private room for study
IM abbreviates Institute of Management

explanation.surface: A course of study is backed by a management body.
explanation.definitionFit: A sturdy cotton twill fabric used for jeans is a cloth, or material.

clue.text: Rodent clubbed without state resistance

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, the clubbing word wraps around the rest

parts.note: to club is to beat
to aver is to state firmly
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A rodent is beaten up despite showing no political resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: BEAT surrounds AVER and R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian water rat, a large semi-aquatic rodent, is also known by this name.

clue.text: A success in time past

parts.note: to make a go of something is to make it a success

explanation.surface: A triumph in former days.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means before now, back in earlier days.

clue.text: Dimwit finding place to stay in city

indicators.note: the lodging is placed inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York City
an inn offers rooms for travellers

explanation.surface: A fool goes looking for a hotel room in the big city.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton or fool; a silly, foolish person is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Medicine unknown morbid condition needed

parts.note: drops are a liquid medicine, as for eyes or ears
y is one of the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: A doctor needs an unidentified medicine for a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for oedema, a swelling from fluid retention, which is an illness.

clue.text: Decorate sort of knitwear for a craft

parts.note: to trim a garment is to decorate it
Aran is a style of chunky knitted jumper from the Aran Islands of Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone embellishes a cable-knit jumper as a handicraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like knitting work but means a vessel. An Aran is a thick patterned wool jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat with three parallel hulls is a type of sailing vessel, which 'craft' means.
